sm: The piece argues that heavy government protection makes people less safe and less prosperous, drawing on economist Allison Schrager's book Worth The Risk. Tightrope walker Nik Wallenda says regulations scare him more than his stunts, and he fears they will bankrupt the circus he bought. Schrager says young people raised to expect guarantees feel they can't get ahead, and that workers who stay in jobs they dislike miss the raises that come from changing jobs. The segment contrasts Europe, with its many regulators, hard-to-fire workers, debts and slow growth, against America, where bankruptcy rules let risk-takers like Donald Trump, Henry Ford and Milton Hershey fail and try again. It closes by criticizing socialist promises of guaranteed jobs and arguing that economic growth, not excessive safety rules, makes lives better.
